fixes.explanation: True, baker! The veil is made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it (Exodus 36:35). The ten curtains got the same treatment (Exodus 36:8). Same fancy yarn, same cherubim. I couldn't even keep a stamp lined up in a junk drawer, and these folks are weaving angels into cloth.

A lion? Ooh, I like the confidence, friend, but no. Bezalel makes two cherubim of hammered gold for the ends of the mercy seat (Exodus 37:7). Not a lion in sight. One cherub goes on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold (Exodus 37:8).

An eagle, huh? Nice try, baker, but the wings on this one belong to somebody else. At the ends of the mercy seat, Bezalel hammers out two cherubim of gold (Exodus 37:7). The text says one cherub is on one end and one on the other (Exodus 37:8). Two ends, two cherubim, and no eagles anywhere in that verse.

You got it, baker! Look at that pose. The wings spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat, and the two cherubim face each other, looking toward the mercy seat (Exodus 37:9). Two gold figures, wings up, and their eyes on the same spot. That's some serious focus. I can't even keep my eyes on one cookie.

Right, baker! Nobody is gluing anything on here. Bezalel hammers the lampstand out of pure gold, and the buds and branches come out as part of it (Exodus 37:22). Then verse 17 says the whole lampstand is all of one piece (Exodus 37:17). If I had to hammer that from a single lump, I'd have flat gold and a very sore mustache.
